structured.answer: I'd go with the second one, the one that says in plain Hebrew what's inside each index, like "חמש מאות החברות הגדולות בארצות הברית" next to S&P 500. In the first one, "ת"א-90" and "MSCI AC World" are just names to me. I'm fairly sure, but neither one helped me understand what the fees actually cost me.

stuck.where: Fees column on the far left, both screens
stuck.why: Each fund has three percentages, קבוע, משתנה and נאמן. I don't know if I should add them up or which one is the real fee. I just looked at the big one: 0.8% for S&P 500.

stuck.where: Badges under the fund names (S&P 500 and MSCI rows)
stuck.why: 'עסקת החלף' and 'מס גם על שינויי המטבע' sound like something risky or extra. I didn't get them, and the tax one scared me a bit about the S&P fund, which is the one I came for.
'ת"א-90' and 'MSCI AC World' told me nothing. I couldn't tell what's in them, so I'd have skipped those funds.

used: On screen 2, the one-line descriptions under each index, e.g. 'חמש מאות החברות הגדולות בארצות הברית', 'מאה עשרים וחמש החברות בעלות השווי הגבוה ביותר בבורסה בתל אביב'

findings.what: Three separate fee percentages per fund with no total and no shekel amount. I can't tell what I'd really pay, and a small % sounds like nothing to me anyway.
findings.where: Fees column, far left, both options

findings.what: The fees sit at the far left end of the row. Reading from the right, I nearly missed them.
In option 1 the index is only a name. Without the description I don't know what ת"א-90 or MSCI AC World holds.
Jargon badges like עסקת החלף, צוברת and the tax-on-currency one aren't explained and make the S&P fund feel risky.
findings.where: Under fund names, S&P 500 and MSCI rows
